claims.claim: Mutual/cross-calibration between the Hall and coil channels is direction-dependent and only partly feasible, not a symmetric "the sensors calibrate each other" relationship. Hall->coil correction of the coil chain's integrator drift/leakage/initial condition is the only hardware-proven direction (demonstrated outside fusion in a CERN bench context and deployed at ITER's OVSS system). Coil->Hall is only conditionally feasible, and only for gain (via a trusted coil chain plus real field excursions); the coil can never deliver the Hall offset, because a constant Hall offset is observationally identical to a static field shift the coil cannot see -- offset recovery requires zero-field (or known-field) epochs or an external absolute reference. If both Hall and coil parameters drift simultaneously and unreferenced, the pair has a proven two-parameter blind spot: it can detect that the two channels disagree but cannot attribute which channel drifted.

claims.limitation: REFINEMENT (full run, better evidence found): the full sweep located the source document's own formal derivation this plain-language claim summarizes -- 02_OBSERVABILITY_AND_IDENTIFIABILITY.md's "Theorem 1" is labeled by the source itself as Derived mathematics (not Inferred): for any unreferenced Hall+coil pair with constant gains/offsets, a two-dimensional symmetry-group transformation (scale factor alpha, offset shift beta) leaves every possible measurement identical, so no excitation whatsoever can break it; this is confirmed numerically by a reproducible Fisher-information rank test (tools/observability_rank_tests.py, CASE A: rank 5 of 7, both null directions matched to the source's stated ~1e-15 residual). The label 'inferred' is kept on this claim per the task's instruction to keep C01-C10 IDs and substance stable; the underlying mathematics is more rigorously supported (Derived, with a numerical structural demonstration) than 'inferred' alone conveys -- see new claim C23 for the formal statement. As before: the source states explicitly "no hardware demonstration of the coil->Hall direction exists in fusion conditions," the one real-world coil->Hall gain-tracking precedent it cites is a single non-fusion, unirradiated, driven-ramp source, and folder 08 (the source mission) has not passed its own redteam/synthesis stages.

claims.claim: The proposed hybrid architecture treats bandwidth fusion as a distinct design element from calibration: the Hall channel is proposed to supply the DC/low-frequency field content the coil cannot see (the coil measures dB/dt and is blind at steady field), while an embedded calibration-winding injection scheme is proposed to be placed in an "overlap band" -- above the drift band, below the Hall sensor's dynamic pole, and inside the coil's flat response -- so that injecting near/above the Hall pole can identify Hall dynamics (pole/delay) that neither channel could establish alone at low frequency.
claims.opt2_mapping: Opt2 Element 2: integrate Hall + inductive coils as a hybrid diagnostic (bandwidth-fusion claim, kept distinct from absolute calibration C06, mutual consistency C07, and radiation compensation C09)
claims.page_or_section: "Hall -> coil" bullet; frequency-plan detail in 03_RADIATION_COMPENSATION_ARCHITECTURE.md Section 5.2; formal Case 9 (fast transient / overlap band) derivation in 02_OBSERVABILITY_AND_IDENTIFIABILITY.md Section 5.9
claims.limitation: REFINEMENT (full run): the full sweep found the Case-9 formal derivation this design claim rests on: with excitation near/above the Hall pole and a trusted coil chain, Hall dynamics (pole, delay) become identifiable (numerical CASE H-broad: rank 5/6); moving all excitation content a decade below the pole collapses the pole-carrying singular value by an order of magnitude (CASE H-narrow), so near-DC operation cannot verify Hall bandwidth at all -- directly reinforcing why C05's unverified 1 MHz figure blocks any bandwidth-fusion design today. No bandwidth-fusion hardware test has been run.
